summary.text: Ben Cline is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Virginia's 6th District, seeking a fifth term. A Virginia attorney who began his career on the staff of Rep. Bob Goodlatte, he served 16 years in the Virginia House of Delegates and worked as an assistant Commonwealth's attorney before winning the seat Goodlatte vacated in 2018. He sits on the Judiciary, Appropriations, Intelligence and Budget committees.

paragraphs.text: Cline was born in Stillwater, Oklahoma, in 1972. His official biography says he grew up in Rockbridge County, Virginia, and graduated from Lexington High School in 1990.
He earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Bates College in 1994 and a J.D. from the University of Richmond in 2007.
He began working for Rep. Bob Goodlatte on his legislative staff in 1994 and ultimately served as his Chief of Staff; Ballotpedia lists this service as 1994 to 2002.
According to Ballotpedia, he then served as president of New Dominion Solutions LLC from 2002 to 2007.
Cline served in the Virginia House of Delegates for the 24th District from 2002 to 2018, where he chaired the Committee on Militia, Police, and Public Safety.
He also worked as an attorney in private practice and was an Assistant Commonwealth's Attorney for Rockingham County and the City of Harrisonburg from 2007 to 2013.

Cline won the open 6th District seat in 2018 to succeed Goodlatte and took office January 3, 2019. In the current Congress he is a member of the House Judiciary, Appropriations, Permanent Select Intelligence and Budget committees.
According to his official biography, he lives in Botetourt County with his wife, Elizabeth, and their two daughters.
